items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I mean Clifford Brown was a leader, he died what when he was 25, 26 years old when he died, but he was really a leader.

ctx.x: Do you feel that some young jazz musicians become leaders too soon?

Oh you get me started on this. Yes obviously. I mean Clifford Brown was a leader, he died what when he was 25, 26 years old when he died, but he was really a leader. He was a very responsible young man. To this day LaRue, his widow, Clifford was the kind of guy, they were buying a home when he died, and he had homeowner’s insurance, life insurance, that’s the kind of responsibility he had. I mean he understood if he did die then the house would be paid for, and that’s what happened. So I mean he had that kind of…
Is this whole thing here with the jazz convention and jazz education, is that in any way messing with the evolution?
